name: MMStar
description: MMStar is an elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans. It benchmarks 6 core capabilities (Coarse Perception, Fine-grained Perception, Instance Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Science & Technology, Mathematics) and 18 detailed axes, aiming to evaluate LVLMs' multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples that exhibit visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and require advanced multi-modal capabilities.
creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao (University of Science and Technology of China, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shanghai AI Laboratory)
citeAs: Chen et al., 'Are We on the Right Way for Evaluating Large Vision-Language Models?', Shanghai AI Laboratory, 2024.
rai:dataCollection: Samples were first roughly selected from existing multi-modal benchmarks (MMBench, SEED-Bench, MMMU, ScienceQA, AI2D, MathVista) using an automated pipeline with LLM inspectors to filter out visually unnecessary or leaked samples, followed by strict manual review by three experts to ensure visual dependency, coverage of capability dimensions, and requirement of advanced multi-modal abilities.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Samples sourced from six existing multi-modal benchmarks: MMBench (focused on natural images), SEED-Bench (focused on natural images), MMMU (college-level subjects), ScienceQA, AI2D, and MathVista (scientific and technical knowledge). The initial pool comprised 22,401 samples.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Some samples were transformed from uni-modal to multi-modal formats to prevent LLMs from recalling correct answers, ensuring minimal data leakage.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An automated coarse filtering pipeline was applied using 8 LLM inspectors (2 closed-source: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro; 6 open-source: LLaMA-70B, Qwen-1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B, InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Deepseek-67B) with a 2-shot in-context inference strategy. Samples answerable by more than 2 of the 8 LLMs were excluded. This reduced the pool from 22,401 to 11,607 candidate samples. Then 16 leading LVLMs were used to gauge difficulty and split samples into four levels (easy: 12-16 hits, moderate: 8-11, hard: 4-7, tough: 0-3). All questions were converted into multiple-choice format.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three experts conducted manual review of the 11,607 coarsely filtered samples to ensure: (1) each sample's answer requires understanding of visual content; (2) selected samples cover a comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions; (3) most samples require LVLMs to possess advanced multi-modal abilities. Samples were split into four difficulty categories based on LVLM hit counts. Final selection of 1,500 high-quality samples considered both diversity of capability dimensions and difficulty levels.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Difficulty levels were determined by tallying hit counts of 16 LVLMs on coarsely filtered samples: easy (12-16 hits), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3). LLM performance on MMStar was found to be nearly indistinguishable from random choice, validating significant visual dependency and minimal data leakage.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Three domain experts conducted the manual review; no further demographic details provided.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Eight LLM inspectors used for automated filtering: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro (closed-source); LLaMA2-70B, Qwen-1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B, InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Deepseek-67B (open-source). Sixteen LVLMs used for difficulty assessment including GPT4V, GeminiPro-Vision, LLaVA series. VLMEvalKit used as evaluation codebase.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage into LLM and LVLM training corpora.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MMStar addresses critical issues in LVLM evaluation—visual content unnecessity and unintentional data leakage—that can lead to misjudgments of actual multi-modal capabilities and potentially misguide LVLM research. By providing a fair and reliable benchmark, it aims to advance the field of multi-modal language model research and ensure more transparent and equitable model comparisons.
rai:dataBiases: The benchmark is constructed from existing benchmarks which may carry their own biases. The selection process focuses on samples requiring visual understanding, which may skew toward certain types of visual content or tasks covered by the source benchmarks (MMBench, SEED-Bench, MMMU, ScienceQA, AI2D, MathVista).
rai:dataLimitations: MMStar contains only 1,500 samples, which may limit comprehensive coverage. The benchmark is static and may become susceptible to data leakage over time as new LLMs and LVLMs are trained on larger corpora. The source benchmarks are limited to six existing benchmarks, potentially missing other important evaluation dimensions.
rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) on multi-modal capabilities. The benchmark is designed to assess actual multi-modal gains rather than LLM backbone capabilities, using Accuracy, Multi-modal Gain (MG), and Multi-modal Leakage (ML) metrics. It covers 6 core capabilities: Coarse Perception, Fine-grained Perception, Instance Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Science & Technology, and Mathematics.
